positions.as_written: Expect disagreement between calculated and directly measured joint loads, and quote both when the difference matters.
Treat sectioning study figures as order dependent, since the sequence of cutting changes the apportionment.
Read a biomechanical claim with its method and its date attached, as a matter of habit rather than scepticism.
Expect any sectioning study's apportionment to depend on cutting order, and read several rather than one.
Treat a figure that has no method attached as unusable, however often it is repeated.
Consider which of your own standard figures come from an era whose instruments could not have measured what the figure claims.
